ground_truth.mitigation: Consider using the TWAP price instead of the spot price.
ground_truth.title: [M-01] `PanopticFactory` uses spot price when deploying new pools, resulting in liquidity manipulation when minting

predictions.description: PanopticPool.liquidate checks the AMM spot against the TWAP before burning the liquidatee's positions, but then burns with unrestricted tick limits using Constants.MIN_V3POOL_TICK and Constants.MAX_V3POOL_TICK. The burn path can execute SFPM.swapInAMM, which directly swaps against Uniswap and changes slot0().tick. Afterward, liquidate reads finalTick and passes it to PanopticMath.getLiquidationBonus and PanopticMath.haircutPremia for cross-token bonus, protocol-loss, and premium-haircut conversions. It also passes finalTick as both currentTick and atTick to _checkSolvencyAtTick for the liquidator. No post-burn TWAP/deviation check, price-impact bound, or independent-oracle valuation constrains finalTick before these financial outcomes are calculated. Thus, when the burned position causes a sufficiently large AMM price movement, the liquidation bonus composition and the liquidator's solvency assessment depend on the resulting attacker-influenceable spot price rather than the protected TWAP.
predictions.impact: A liquidation-induced price movement can alter the amount and token composition of liquidation compensation and premium haircuts. It can also make a liquidator's collateral or remaining positions appear solvent at finalTick even if they would fail at the liquidation TWAP, potentially transferring value from the liquidatee, collateral providers, or protocol and leaving post-liquidation bad debt. The supplied source does not provide deployment-specific liquidity or position sizes, so the magnitude of any price movement cannot be quantified.
predictions.mitigation: Use the validated liquidation TWAP, or another independently validated oracle price, for liquidation bonus, haircut, and liquidator-solvency calculations. Alternatively, after all liquidation burns and swaps, enforce a post-operation deviation check between finalTick and the liquidation TWAP before using finalTick, and apply an explicit maximum price-impact/slippage bound to liquidation-induced swaps. The liquidator should additionally be required to satisfy solvency at the independent TWAP or a conservative oracle valuation.
predictions.title: Liquidation payouts and liquidator solvency use an unvalidated post-burn spot price

predictions.description: PanopticPool.forceExercise uses getUniV3TWAP only to determine whether the position is exercisable, but captures the instantaneous Uniswap slot0().tick as currentTick and passes it to CollateralTracker.exerciseCost. No spot/TWAP deviation or independent-price check is applied. CollateralTracker.exerciseCost computes maxNumRangesFromStrike from currentTick and applies an exponentially decaying fee using FORCE_EXERCISE_COST >> (maxNumRangesFromStrike - 1). It also uses currentTick to compare current liquidity values with the TWAP values. An attacker can temporarily move the underlying AMM spot while leaving the TWAP sufficiently unchanged, then call forceExercise; the position can remain exercisable at the TWAP while the manipulated spot increases its apparent distance from the strike and reduces the fee paid to the exercisee.
predictions.impact: The forced-exercise caller can pay less compensation than intended, reducing the refund received by the exercisee. The difference can be captured by the caller and the exercisee can be underpaid. The source does not establish a particular deployment's achievable price displacement, but it shows the complete path from mutable AMM spot state to the forced-exercise fee and settlement amount.
predictions.mitigation: Calculate the forced-exercise fee using the manipulation-resistant TWAP or another independently validated reference tick instead of raw slot0().tick. If the current spot is retained for any calculation, enforce a spot/TWAP deviation bound before calculating and settling the fee, and ensure any AMM state changes during the burn cannot invalidate that bound.
predictions.title: Forced-exercise compensation is calculated from an unvalidated spot tick

ground_truth.description: PanopticPool.pokeOracle() is permissionless and passes the current Uniswap pool tick to RiskEngine.computeInternalMedian(). OraclePack.computeInternalMedian() records the observation only when the current epoch differs from the recorded epoch. An attacker can manipulate the pool's current tick before an update, cause that value to be clamped and inserted into the internal oracle, and prevent later calls in the same epoch from replacing it. Repeating this across epochs can progressively move the oracle away from the legitimate market price.
ground_truth.impact: Manipulating the internal oracle causes positions to be evaluated at incorrect prices, which can produce incorrect solvency validations, unfair liquidations, or allow insolvent positions to remain active.
ground_truth.mitigation: Update the oracle continuously with the current tick as time progresses, similar to a Uniswap TWAP, instead of allowing only one update per epoch. Alternatively, restrict pokeOracle() to trusted callers or use a commit-reveal scheme to prevent frontrunning.
ground_truth.title: [M-11] An attacker can manipulate oracle easily

ground_truth.description: RiskEngine.twapEMA() destructures OraclePack.getEMAs() in the wrong order: it treats the returned (spotEMA, fastEMA, slowEMA, eonsEMA, medianTick) tuple as (eonsEMA, slowEMA, fastEMA, ...). The intended weighted TWAP therefore uses the wrong EMA values, includes the spot EMA in place of the eons EMA, and omits the eons EMA. PanopticPool.getTWAP() uses this value in liquidation and force-exercise checks, so rapid adverse price movements can leave the TWAP near a stale value and cause an unhealthy account to appear solvent at that check.
ground_truth.impact: Unhealthy accounts can appear solvent at that tick and block liquidation/force-exercise (`NotMarginCalled`), delaying cleanup and risking larger bad debt or mispriced exercises/settlements.
ground_truth.mitigation: Destructure the EMAs in the correct order so the intended fast/slow/eons weighting is applied, and add a regression test proving that twapEMA uses those three EMAs rather than the spot EMA.
ground_truth.title: [M-03] TWAP misweights EMAs in RiskEngine, anchoring liquidation price to slow EMA and letting insolvent accounts dodge liquidation

ground_truth.description: When riskParameters.feeRecipient() is zero, CollateralTracker.settleMint() and settleBurn() burn shares from the option owner without removing the corresponding assets. This decreases totalSupply while leaving totalAssets approximately unchanged, immediately increasing the share value for holders at that moment. RiskEngine maps builderCode == 0 to address(0), and PanopticPool's liquidation and force-exercise paths request getRiskParameters(0), so a searcher can deposit before a commission-burn event and exit after it to capture value intended for incumbent liquidity providers.
ground_truth.impact: Just-In-Time entrants can capture commission distributions intended for longer-term liquidity providers. A sufficiently dominant entrant can also reduce the effective commission through fee self-rebating, weakening the fee model and LP incentives.
ground_truth.mitigation: Avoid instantaneous burn-based commission distribution. Treat builderCode == 0 as a non-zero protocol or treasury recipient, or distribute commissions through a time-weighted or streamed mechanism; any cooldown must also account for transfers so it cannot be bypassed.
ground_truth.title: [M-15] Commission share-burn distribution is JIT-capturable when `builderCode == 0` (default)
